meta.title: Investigation Ontology (Demo)
meta.description: A minimal vocabulary for AML investigation records, built to demonstrate how business data can point into AMLO and AML typology. An extension: not part of AMLO or AML typology.
meta.note: Not a standard and not complete. The namespace is a placeholder.

classes.label: Alert
classes.comment: A flag raised by monitoring (a rule, a model or a graph analysis) on some activity.

classes.label: Case
classes.comment: An investigation opened on one or more alerts.

classes.label: Checklist item
classes.comment: One suggested line of enquiry for an alert: an AML typology indicator to look into, why it matters for this alert, how urgent it is, and which kind of records would show it. Advice only: no data is queried.

classes.label: Evidence
classes.comment: A piece of material gathered for an alert or case. Its kind is given by inv:recordType, an AML typology data source type.

classes.label: Finding
classes.comment: An investigator's assessment of one AML typology indicator within a case.

classes.label: Paragraph
classes.comment: One paragraph of a report draft, tied to the findings it rests on.

classes.label: Report draft
classes.comment: A draft narrative for a case. It always requires investigator review.

properties.label: based on
properties.comment: The findings a paragraph rests on.

properties.label: hypothesis
properties.comment: An AML typology technique the case is investigating.

properties.label: indicator
properties.comment: The AML typology indicator a checklist item or finding is about.

properties.label: paragraphs
properties.comment: The ordered paragraphs of a report draft (an rdf:List).

properties.label: record type
properties.comment: The kind of record the evidence is: an AML typology data source.

properties.label: suggested data source
properties.comment: An AML typology data source (a type of record) the investigator should look at for the indicator.

properties.label: suspected technique
properties.comment: The AML typology technique an alert is suspected to involve. A hypothesis, not a conclusion.

properties.label: technique
properties.comment: The AML typology technique a finding is made under.

properties.label: priority
properties.comment: Order in which to look into the suggestions for one alert. 1 is first.

properties.label: reason
properties.comment: Why this indicator is worth checking for this alert, in the adviser's words. Advice, not a finding.

properties.label: source id
properties.comment: The identifier the record has in the source system.

properties.label: status
properties.comment: Whether the indicator was supported, not supported, inconclusive, or could not be assessed.

properties.label: trigger reason
properties.comment: Why the monitoring system raised the alert, as stated by that system.

rules.message: An alert needs exactly one alert id.
An alert needs exactly one raised-at timestamp (xsd:dateTime).

rules.rule: at least one, of type xsd:string
rules.message: An alert needs the reason the monitoring system raised it.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to amlo:Technique
rules.message: An alert needs at least one suspected technique, and it must be an AML typology technique.
hasEvidence must point to Evidence.
A case needs exactly one case id.
A case needs exactly one opened-at timestamp.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to amlo:Technique
rules.message: A case needs at least one hypothesis, and it must be an AML typology technique.
A checklist item belongs to exactly one alert.
A checklist item is about exactly one AML typology indicator.

rules.rule: exactly one, of type xsd:integer, at least 1
rules.message: A checklist item needs exactly one priority, a whole number from 1 upwards.
A checklist item needs a reason why the indicator matters for this alert.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to amlo:DataSource
rules.message: A checklist item must suggest at least one data source to look at, and it must be an AML typology data source.
Evidence needs exactly one record type, and it must be an AML typology data source.
A finding is made under exactly one AML typology technique.
A finding is about exactly one AML typology indicator.

rules.rule: exactly one, one of: supported, not-supported, inconclusive, not-assessable
rules.message: status must be supported, not-supported, inconclusive or not-assessable.

rules.rule: at least one, of type xsd:string
rules.message: A finding needs an observation.
A supported finding must cite the evidence it rests on.
A paragraph needs exactly one text.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to inv:Finding
rules.message: Every paragraph must be based on at least one finding.
A report draft belongs to exactly one case.
A report draft needs a review status.
A report draft needs one ordered list of paragraphs.

consistency: a checklist item's indicator does not belong to the alert's suspected technique
a checklist item suggests a data source that AML typology does not list for the alert's suspected technique
a finding's indicator does not belong to the finding's technique
a finding is made under a technique the case is not investigating
a report paragraph rests on a finding that is not part of the report's case

@graph.trigger_reason: Graph analysis: funds moved through 5 accounts and returned to the origin within 5.2 days

@graph.reason: The alert itself describes funds returning to the origin account, which is the core of this indicator.
A ring of five accounts raises the question of who owns them and whether they were opened close together.
If the accounts belong to trading companies, the circular flow may be backed by repeated shipments and invoices.

@graph.observation: Funds left account A-01 and returned to it through four intermediate accounts within 5.2 days.
No ownership or onboarding data was available, so this indicator was not assessed.

paragraphs.text: Transaction records show a circular movement of funds consistent with Circular Transactions (T0039): the funds returned to the originating account within 5.2 days (IND02191).
Indicator IND02194 could not be assessed because ownership and onboarding data was not available.
